title: The rollup's tag-activation check cannot work from a member account
description:
Found 2026-09-30 after the AWS reorg (peer session 'Rearrange AWS accounts'). The old workload account is now a MEMBER of a new Organization, and only the management account may manage cost allocation tags.

## Evidence
- Invoked chatticus-development-daily-budget-rollup from the legacy (member) account. It logged: tenant_tag_lookup_failed reason=AccessDeniedException ... ListCostAllocationTags: 'Linked account doesn't have access to cost allocation tags.' The same call from the management profile succeeds (empty list; Cost Explorer was just enabled there and needs about 24h).
- cost_explorer.py (#372) asks ce:ListCostAllocationTags whether chatticus:tenant is active, and treats any failed lookup as NOT active (fail closed, ce_status=error). That was right while the workload account was the management account; it cannot succeed from a member account.

## Effect
Safe (fails closed) but permanent: after the tags are activated in the management account (d706d7), hosted organizations would still read error, so the meter never becomes real for them.

## Constraint found while looking for a replacement
ce:GetTags works from the linked account. For an inactive tag it returns only [""] (the empty value). It would return real values once a tag is active and tagged resources have billed. But chatticus:tenant only gets real values after a tenant-tagged computer task has run, so a hosted organization with a ceiling that has never run a computer would read as not active and be refused its first computer (chicken and egg). No hosted organization has a ceiling today (customer-account organizations are read another way), so this is latent, not live.

## Options (needs a decision; do not build until the tags are active and the positive case can be observed)
1. Replace the check with ce:GetTags on chatticus:tenant (values present means active). Keep fail closed. Accept the first-computer chicken and egg, or
2. Drop per-tenant liveness from the check and use an installation-wide tag (chatticus:installation or environment) as the 'tags are active' signal, since the operator activates them together; an absent tenant then reads as a real zero, or
3. Make the activation an explicit deploy-time setting the operator flips when done.
Recommend 2.

## Done when
After activation in the management account, a hosted organization's rollup row reads ok with a real figure from the member account, and the decision on the chicken and egg is recorded.
